domain: Network, connectivity, and radio telemetry (iOS 26 shipping / iOS 27 developer beta 4 as of July 2026) — personal sideloaded quantified-self app

capabilities.stream: Network path status (satisfied / unsatisfied / requiresConnection) and every change event
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven; callback fires on every path change. No polling limit while process is alive.
capabilities.notes: NWPathMonitor also has init(requiredInterfaceType:) and init(prohibitedInterfaceTypes:), plus .queue and .cancel(). Runs only while your process runs; iOS suspends you within ~30s of backgrounding unless you hold a background mode. Cheapest, most permissionless stream in the whole domain.

capabilities.stream: Active interface type of the current path (Wi-Fi vs cellular vs wired vs loopback vs other)
capabilities.api: NWPath.usesInterfaceType(_:) and NWPath.availableInterfaces; NWInterface.InterfaceType cases (COMPLETE, 5 total): .wifi, .cellular, .wiredEthernet, .loopback, .other
capabilities.notes: That is the entire enum — there is no .bluetooth, no .vpn, no .hotspot case. VPN and AWDL both surface as .other. Apple Watch reports its own path independently.

capabilities.stream: BSD interface names of every available interface (en0, pdp_ip0/pdp_ip1, utun*, ipsec*, awdl0, llw0, bridge100, ap1, lo0)
capabilities.notes: Highest-leverage free signal in this domain. Names let you infer, with zero entitlement: VPN/tunnel active (utun*/ipsec*/ppp*), AirDrop/AirPlay/Continuity peer-to-peer activity (awdl0), Personal Hotspot being SHARED by this device (bridge100 / ap1 present), and dual-SIM data-SIM identity (pdp_ip0 vs pdp_ip1). CAVEAT: Apple DTS states BSD interface names are not formally API on Apple platforms (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/49581) — treat as heuristic, not contract.

capabilities.stream: Expensive-interface flag (on cellular OR tethered to a Personal Hotspot)
capabilities.notes: Apple's own abstract: 'an interface that is considered expensive, such as Cellular or a Personal Hotspot.' Therefore usesInterfaceType(.wifi) && isExpensive == true is a documented, free, permissionless detector for 'I am tethered to someone's hotspot' — distinct from bridge100 existing, which means 'I am the one sharing.'

capabilities.stream: Low Data Mode flag (per-network user setting)
capabilities.notes: Reflects the user's per-Wi-Fi-network / per-cellular-plan Low Data Mode toggle — a behavioral signal about the user, not just the link.

capabilities.stream: Ultra-constrained flag (new user-preference constraint tier)
capabilities.notes: NEW in iOS 26 (26.0 across iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS). Verified on the per-symbol page — the NWPath list page misreports it as iOS 12.

capabilities.stream: Link-quality measurement of the link-layer attachment
capabilities.notes: NEW in iOS 26. Closest legitimate public proxy to 'signal bars' you will ever get. Apple's discussion warns: 'Use this value to tune initial values for algorithms... Do not use this value to gate connection attempts.' Nothing stops you logging it.

capabilities.stream: Reason the path is unusable (which radio/permission is the blocker)
capabilities.notes: .vpnInactive is the only free, permissionless, Apple-blessed VPN signal — it fires when an always-on/on-demand VPN is required but down. .localNetworkDenied is the closest thing to a local-network-permission status API (see blockers).

capabilities.stream: Protocol support on the current path (IPv4 / IPv6 / DNS configured)
capabilities.notes: IPv6-only networks are a decent carrier/venue fingerprint (T-Mobile US, most enterprise guest Wi-Fi).

capabilities.stream: Gateway endpoints of the attached network (router addresses)
capabilities.notes: Free, entitlement-less partial substitute for BSSID place-fingerprinting: the gateway set differs between networks. Low entropy alone (192.168.1.1 everywhere) — combine with the interface-name set, supportsIPv6, and Bonjour results to build a stable per-place hash.

capabilities.stream: Local and remote endpoint of a specific connection
capabilities.notes: localEndpoint gives your own current LAN IP without touching getifaddrs or local-network permission.

capabilities.stream: Wi-Fi Aware path status/performance on a connection
capabilities.permission: none beyond Wi-Fi Aware's own pairing flow
capabilities.notes: nil unless the path is over Wi-Fi Aware. Paid-team only (see Wi-Fi Aware entry).

capabilities.stream: Current radio access technology per cellular service (5G NR / 5G NSA / LTE / etc.)
capabilities.api: CTTelephonyNetworkInfo.serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology -> [String: String]. Values are the 13 CTRadioAccessTechnology constants (COMPLETE LIST): CTRadioAccessTechnologyGPRS, CTRadioAccessTechnologyEdge, CTRadioAccessTechnologyWCDMA, CTRadioAccessTechnologyHSDPA, CTRadioAccessTechnologyHSUPA, CTRadioAccessTechnologyCDMA1x, CTRadioAccessTechnologyCDMAEVDORev0, CTRadioAccessTechnologyCDMAEVDORevA, CTRadioAccessTechnologyCDMAEVDORevB, CTRadioAccessTechnologyeHRPD, CTRadioAccessTechnologyLTE, CTRadioAccessTechnologyNRNSA, CTRadioAccessTechnologyNR
capabilities.notes: NOT deprecated — the one CoreTelephony stream that survived the iOS 16 privacy purge intact, needing no permission and no entitlement. Dictionary keys are opaque per-SIM service IDs. Entry is nil when that service is not registered on any network — a clean 'no service' detector. CONTESTED: forum reports that CTServiceRadioAccessTechnologyDidChangeNotification fires late or inaccurately (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/691737); mitigate by polling the dictionary on a timer as well as observing.

capabilities.stream: Which SIM is currently carrying data (dual-SIM / eSIM switch events)
capabilities.notes: Free travel/roaming proxy: switching to a travel eSIM changes this identifier. Combine with pdp_ip0/pdp_ip1 interface names to know which physical PDP context is live.

capabilities.stream: Whether the system has restricted this app's cellular data
capabilities.notes: Reads the user's per-app Cellular Data toggle in Settings. Distinguishes 'no cellular data' from 'no cellular signal'. Initial value is often .restrictedStateUnknown briefly after launch.

capabilities.stream: Carrier name, MCC, MNC, ISO country, VoIP support — DEAD
capabilities.minIOS: deprecated iOS 16.0; hollowed for apps built with the iOS 16.4 SDK or later
capabilities.notes: VERIFIED STILL DEAD THROUGH iOS 26/27. Apple's iOS 16.4 beta 3 release note: 'CTCarrier, a deprecated API, returns static values for apps that are built with the iOS 16.4 SDK or later. (76283818)'. Observed static values: carrierName and isoCountryCode = '--', mobileCountryCode and mobileNetworkCode = '65535'. Header: CORETELEPHONY_CLASS_DEPRECATED(4_0, 16_0, "Deprecated with no replacement"). Apple DTS (Quinn), asked for an alternative: 'No. That's what `Deprecated with no replacement` means.' The class is NOT removed, so calls still compile and return — you just get garbage. Do not build a carrier dimension into the schema.

capabilities.stream: Current Wi-Fi network identity: SSID, BSSID, security type
capabilities.permission: CoreLocation authorization at PRECISE accuracy — NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (or Always). Alternatively satisfied by: app configured this network via NEHotspotConfiguration, OR app has active VPN configurations installed, OR app has an active NEDNSSettingsManager configuration.
capabilities.notes: CANNOT BE SIGNED ON A FREE APPLE ID. 'Access WiFi information' is checked only in the ADP and ADEP columns of Apple's capability table — the free 'Apple Developer' column is blank. This one line decides the whole Wi-Fi half of the project: $99/yr or no SSID. Apple verbatim: 'This method also requires the app to have the Access Wi-Fi Information Entitlement, and produces nil if the app lacks this entitlement.' Also: fetchCurrent populates ONLY ssid/bssid/securityType — 'This call doesn't populate other fields in the object', so signalStrength, didAutoJoin, didJustJoin, isChosenHelper stay empty.

capabilities.stream: Current Wi-Fi SSID/BSSID via the legacy Captive Network API
capabilities.api: CNCopySupportedInterfaces(), CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo(_:) -> keys kCNNetworkInfoKeySSID, kCNNetworkInfoKeyBSSID, kCNNetworkInfoKeySSIDData
capabilities.permission: same as above (precise location since iOS 13)
capabilities.notes: Apple's entitlement doc still describes the entitlement in terms of CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo. Deprecated in favour of NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent; same paid entitlement, so no advantage. Listed for completeness of the enumeration.

capabilities.stream: Rich Wi-Fi network metadata: signalStrength, isSecure, didAutoJoin, didJustJoin, isChosenHelper
capabilities.api: NEHotspotNetwork.signalStrength (Double 0.0–1.0), .isSecure, .didAutoJoin, .didJustJoin, .isChosenHelper — populated ONLY inside an NEHotspotHelper command callback
capabilities.resolution: Delivered on helper commands (Evaluate/Authenticate/Maintain), not pollable
capabilities.notes: Background execution uses UIBackgroundModes 'network-authentication'. EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE: paid team AND manual Apple approval at developer.apple.com/contact/request/hotspot-helper. Apple DTS: 'The vast majority of Hotspot Helper requests are rejected because they are not a support use case for the API' and 'NEHotspotHelper is only useful for hotspot integration. There are both technical and business restrictions that prevent it from being used for other tasks, such as accessory integration or Wi-Fi based location.' Turnaround weeks to months. A quantified-self app is exactly the use case Apple names as disqualifying.

capabilities.stream: List of Wi-Fi networks this app previously configured
capabilities.notes: Returns ONLY networks your own app configured — not the device's saved-network list, not networks the user added. Paid ('Hotspot' is ADP/ADEP only). Its real value is as the alternate door into fetchCurrent: if your app configured the network, fetchCurrent works without location permission.

capabilities.stream: Per-interface cumulative byte and packet counters (Wi-Fi vs cellular vs tunnel vs AWDL data volume)
capabilities.api: getifaddrs(_:) -> ifaddrs; filter sa_family == AF_LINK; cast ifa_data to struct if_data; read ifi_ibytes, ifi_obytes, ifi_ipackets, ifi_opackets (also ifi_ierrors, ifi_oerrors, ifi_collisions, ifi_iqdrops). Interfaces: en0 (Wi-Fi), pdp_ip0..pdp_ip7 (cellular PDP contexts), utun*/ipsec*/ppp* (tunnels), awdl0 (AirDrop/AirPlay P2P), llw0, bridge100 + ap1 (hotspot sharing), lo0
capabilities.resolution: Poll at any rate (1 Hz is negligible cost); byte-granular
capabilities.backfill: cumulative since last device reboot — first launch returns the whole since-boot total, a real if coarse backfill no other API offers
capabilities.notes: STILL WORKS in iOS 26/27 and is App Store safe (public C API; Apple DTS publishes Swift sample code for it). Apple's stated limits, verbatim: 'The counters reset each time the device restarts' and 'The counters are represented as a UInt32, and so wrap at 4 GiB.' Also 'The <net/if_var.h> header defines an if_data64 structure, but there's no supported way to get that value on Apple platforms.' Handling: sample on a timer, diff, and treat any DECREASE as either a 4 GiB wrap (add 2^32) or a reboot (restart the series) — disambiguate with ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime. Wrap is a daily event on Wi-Fi, not a corner case. Also yields a free reboot-detector and device-uptime series.

capabilities.stream: Supported historical Wi-Fi/cellular data volume for YOUR app (the only Apple-blessed byte counter)
capabilities.api: iOS 13–26: MXMetricManager.shared, MXMetricManagerSubscriber.didReceive(_ payloads:), MXMetricPayload.networkTransferMetrics -> MXNetworkTransferMetric.cumulativeCellularDownload / .cumulativeCellularUpload / .cumulativeWifiDownload / .cumulativeWifiUpload; MXMetricManager.pastPayloads. iOS 27: MetricManager delivering MetricReport via async sequence, read through MetricResult with TotalWiFiDownloadMetric / TotalWiFiUploadMetric / TotalCellularDownloadMetric / TotalCellularUploadMetric
capabilities.minIOS: 13.0 (MXNetworkTransferMetric deprecated in iOS 27.0 in favour of MetricResult)
capabilities.resolution: 24-hour aggregate, delivered at most once per day
capabilities.backfill: MXMetricManager.pastPayloads returns payloads from the past ~7 days, but only those generated while your app was installed — effectively NONE on first launch
capabilities.notes: The system delivers payloads to your app without you holding a background mode. Apple DTS names this as THE supported answer: 'To get network usage for your app, use MetricKit. Specifically, look at the MXNetworkTransferMetric payload.' Zero permission, zero entitlement — free-team compatible. Apple's stated limits: 'You only get metrics for your app' and 'You get metrics periodically; you can't monitor these statistics in real time.' iOS 27 BREAKING CHANGE — build ingestion against both APIs, since 27 ships ~Sept 2026.

capabilities.stream: Per-HTTP-request network attribution and full connection timing
capabilities.api: URLSessionTaskDelegate.urlSession(_:task:didFinishCollecting:) -> URLSessionTaskMetrics.transactionMetrics -> URLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics: .isCellular, .isExpensive, .isConstrained, .isMultipath, .isProxyConnection, .isReusedConnection, .networkProtocolName, .remoteAddress, .remotePort, .localAddress, .localPort, .negotiatedTLSProtocolVersion, .negotiatedTLSCipherSuite, .resourceFetchType, .domainResolutionProtocol, .countOfRequestBodyBytesSent, .countOfRequestHeaderBytesSent, .countOfResponseBodyBytesReceived, .countOfResponseHeaderBytesReceived, .countOfRequestBodyBytesBeforeEncoding, .countOfResponseBodyBytesAfterDecoding, plus 11 timing Dates: fetchStartDate, domainLookupStartDate, domainLookupEndDate, connectStartDate, secureConnectionStartDate, secureConnectionEndDate, connectEndDate, requestStartDate, requestEndDate, responseStartDate, responseEndDate
capabilities.resolution: Per request; millisecond timing, byte-exact counts
capabilities.notes: Covers only requests YOUR app makes — but for a QS app that periodically probes a known endpoint this is a free, permissionless, high-resolution network-quality instrument: DNS latency, TCP handshake, TLS handshake, TTFB, negotiated HTTP version, cellular-or-not. Works with URLSession background configurations.

capabilities.stream: Nearby BLE advertisers — crowd density / proximity proxy (foreground)
capabilities.api: CBCentralManager(delegate:queue:); scanForPeripherals(withServices: nil, options: [CBCentralManagerScanOptionAllowDuplicatesKey: true]); centralManager(_:didDiscover:advertisementData:rssi:). Advertisement keys (COMPLETE, 8): CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey, CBAdvertisementDataManufacturerDataKey, CBAdvertisementDataServiceDataKey, CBAdvertisementDataServiceUUIDsKey, CBAdvertisementDataOverflowServiceUUIDsKey, CBAdvertisementDataSolicitedServiceUUIDsKey, CBAdvertisementDataTxPowerLevelKey, CBAdvertisementDataIsConnectable. Plus RSSI (NSNumber, dBm), CBPeripheral.identifier, CBPeripheral.name
capabilities.permission: NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription (iOS 13+) — one-time runtime prompt. Add NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription only if deployment target < iOS 13.
capabilities.resolution: Continuous while foregrounded with allowDuplicates:true; RSSI per advertisement
capabilities.notes: FREE-TEAM SIGNABLE — no entitlement, just a plist string. Best free 'how crowded is this place' instrument on the device. CEILING: you are counting ADVERTISING DEVICES, not people. iOS and Android rotate BLE addresses (~15 min), CBPeripheral.identifier is scoped to your-app+this-device so there is no cross-session or cross-device identity for strangers' phones, and CBAdvertisementDataOverflowServiceUUIDsKey means Apple devices hide most UUIDs in an overflow area discoverable only by explicitly scanning for them. Practical metric: distinct-identifiers-per-minute + RSSI histogram as a relative index, never an absolute headcount.

capabilities.stream: Nearby BLE advertisers in the BACKGROUND
capabilities.api: Same, but scanForPeripherals(withServices: [explicit CBUUIDs], options:) with UIBackgroundModes containing 'bluetooth-central'; optionally CBCentralManagerOptionRestoreIdentifierKey + centralManager(_:willRestoreState:)
capabilities.entitlement: none (Background Modes IS available to free Personal Teams)
capabilities.resolution: Opportunistic and heavily throttled — 'eventual detection, not immediate responsiveness'
capabilities.notes: Apple verbatim: 'Your app can scan for Bluetooth devices in the background by specifying the bluetooth-central background mode. To do this, your app must explicitly scan for one or more services by specifying them in the serviceUUIDs parameter. The CBCentralManager scan option has no effect while scanning in the background.' So nil-services background scanning returns NOTHING — the crowd-proxy idea collapses in background unless you pre-name service UUIDs. CONTESTED: docs say allowDuplicates has no effect in background; field reports (Punch Through, Uy Nguyen) say extra didDiscover callbacks still arrive when the advertisement payload changes — undocumented, not guaranteed. Scan aggressiveness varies by device model, OS version and battery state via undocumented heuristics.

capabilities.stream: BLE peripherals currently connected to the system (including via other apps)
capabilities.notes: Apple verbatim: 'The list of connected peripherals can include those that other apps have connected.' BUT you must supply service UUIDs — there is no 'give me everything connected' call — so you only find device classes you can name in advance. Enumerating a table of standard SIG service UUIDs (0x180D heart rate, 0x180F battery, 0x1812 HID, 0x1816 cycling speed, 0x1826 fitness machine, …) is the practical technique.

capabilities.stream: Connected audio devices by NAME — AirPods, car head unit, speakers, headphones
capabilities.api: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().currentRoute -> AVAudioSessionRouteDescription; .outputs / .inputs -> [AVAudioSessionPortDescription] with .portType, .portName, .uid, .channels; observe AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification with AVAudioSessionRouteChangeReasonKey. AVAudioSession.Port constants (COMPLETE, 22): inputs — .builtInMic, .headsetMic, .lineIn, .continuityMicrophone; outputs — .builtInSpeaker, .builtInReceiver, .headphones, .lineOut, .airPlay, .HDMI, .bluetoothA2DP, .bluetoothLE, .mediaDeviceExtension; I/O — .bluetoothHFP, .carAudio, .usbAudio, .AVB, .PCI, .displayPort, .fireWire, .thunderbolt, .virtual
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven on every route change; instantaneous
capabilities.notes: Continuous background observation needs UIBackgroundModes 'audio' (free-team signable); otherwise you get route-change events during any runtime window. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO 'ARE CONNECTED BLUETOOTH DEVICES ENUMERABLE' — zero permission, zero entitlement, works on a free Apple ID. portName returns the literal user-visible string ('Zach's AirPods Pro', 'Honda HFT', 'Kitchen HomePod'); portType distinguishes .bluetoothA2DP / .bluetoothHFP / .carAudio / .airPlay. CoreBluetooth CANNOT see any of these — cars, AirPods and most speakers are classic Bluetooth BR/EDR and CoreBluetooth is BLE-only. .carAudio or a known car portName is a de-facto driving detector. Caveat: some Bluetooth INPUTS only appear when the session category is .playAndRecord with .allowBluetooth; outputs are visible more broadly.

capabilities.stream: MFi / Lightning / USB-C wired accessory connection events
capabilities.entitlement: none, but Info.plist must declare UISupportedExternalAccessoryProtocols
capabilities.notes: Background execution uses UIBackgroundModes 'external-accessory'. Only surfaces MFi accessories whose protocol strings you declared in advance — you cannot enumerate arbitrary connected hardware. Marginal for a personal QS app unless you own a specific MFi accessory.

capabilities.stream: Privacy-preserving discovery/pairing of Bluetooth and Wi-Fi accessories without the global permission prompts
capabilities.api: ASAccessorySession, ASDiscoveryDescriptor, ASAccessory (+ ASAccessory.AccessoryState), ASDiscoveredAccessory, ASPickerDisplayItem
capabilities.permission: none of the usual prompts — the picker IS the consent. Info.plist: NSAccessorySetupSupports, NSAccessorySetupBluetoothCompanyIdentifiers, NSAccessorySetupBluetoothNames, NSAccessorySetupBluetoothServices
capabilities.notes: Non-obvious: the sanctioned way to skip the Bluetooth AND Local Network permission prompts entirely for accessories you name up front. Free-team compatible (plist keys only, no entitlement). It narrows rather than broadens visibility — for known devices, not crowd sensing.

capabilities.stream: UWB ranging: distance (metres) and direction to nearby iPhones / Watches / U1-U2 accessories
capabilities.api: NISession, NINearbyPeerConfiguration, NINearbyAccessoryConfiguration, NINearbyObject (.distance, .direction, .discoveryToken, .verticalDirectionEstimate, .horizontalAngle), NISessionDelegate, NIAlgorithmConvergence, NISession.deviceCapabilities (supportsPreciseDistanceMeasurement, supportsDirectionMeasurement, supportsCameraAssistance, supportsExtendedDistanceMeasurement)
capabilities.permission: NSNearbyInteractionUsageDescription (runtime prompt). NSNearbyInteractionAllowOnceUsageDescription is deprecated — do not use in new apps.
capabilities.resolution: ~10 cm distance; direction requires U1/U2 line-of-sight; multi-Hz updates
capabilities.notes: FREE-TEAM SIGNABLE — no entitlement. Requires iPhone 11+ (U1) on BOTH ends and, critically, YOUR app running on both devices (or a UWB accessory implementing NINearbyAccessoryConfiguration). Useless for measuring strangers. Background: by default background UWB ranging works only with Bluetooth-LE-paired-and-connected devices; since iOS 18.4 you can range with any supported device in the background if you start an ActivityKit Live Activity as you background. Either path needs UIBackgroundModes 'nearby-interaction'. Unavailable on visionOS; Mac Catalyst returns supportsPreciseDistanceMeasurement == false.

capabilities.stream: Peer-to-peer discovery of nearby devices running your app (over Wi-Fi, P2P Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth PAN)
capabilities.api: MCNearbyServiceBrowser, MCNearbyServiceAdvertiser, MCSession, MCPeerID, MCBrowserViewController, MCAdvertiserAssistant
capabilities.permission: NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription (runtime local-network prompt) + NSBonjourServices declaring your service types; NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription if BT PAN is used
capabilities.resolution: Discovery events; presence only, no ranging
capabilities.notes: DEPRECATED — all major classes carry deprecation markers. Do not build new work on it; use Network framework's NWBrowser/NetworkBrowser or Wi-Fi Aware. Same fundamental limit as NearbyInteraction: only finds devices running YOUR app.

capabilities.stream: Bonjour/mDNS enumeration of devices and services on the current LAN (router, printers, TVs, HomePods, NAS) — a strong place fingerprint
capabilities.api: iOS 12–25: NWBrowser(for: .bonjour(type:domain:), using:), .browseResultsChangedHandler -> NWBrowser.Result with .endpoint and .metadata (TXT records), plus NWConnection to resolve. iOS 26+: NetworkBrowser (structured-concurrency replacement, alongside NetworkConnection and NetworkListener)
capabilities.permission: NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription + NSBonjourServices array listing every service type you browse (e.g. _airplay._tcp, _raop._tcp, _companion-link._tcp, _homekit._tcp, _ipp._tcp, _http._tcp, _ssh._tcp, _googlecast._tcp)
capabilities.entitlement: none for LISTED Bonjour service types; com.apple.developer.networking.multicast required to browse ARBITRARY service types or send/receive IP multicast/broadcast
capabilities.notes: BEST FREE SUBSTITUTE FOR BSSID PLACE-FINGERPRINTING. You cannot read the SSID on a free account, but you can enumerate the specific set of Bonjour devices present and hash it — home, office and gym produce very different sets, far higher entropy than the gateway IP. Costs one plist string and a one-time runtime prompt. Service types must be enumerated up front; the multicast entitlement that removes that restriction is paid AND requires Apple's approval form at developer.apple.com/contact/request/networking-multicast.

capabilities.stream: Wi-Fi Aware (NAN) peer discovery, pairing, and direct high-bandwidth links with no access point
capabilities.api: WACapabilities, WAPublishableService, WASubscribableService, WAPublisherListener, WASubscriberBrowser, WAPairedDevice, WAEndpoint, WAConnection, WAParameters, WASharedSecret, WAPath, WAPerformanceMode, WAAccessCategory, WAPerformanceReport, WAPerformanceForecast, WAError
capabilities.permission: system pairing flow; Info.plist WiFiAwareServices declaring each service
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.wifi-aware — a String array that must contain 'Publish', 'Subscribe', or both
capabilities.notes: FLAGSHIP iOS 26 NETWORKING ADDITION — and PAID ONLY. It is absent from Apple's supported-capabilities table (verified by grep of the raw page: zero hits for 'Aware'), so the determination rests on the primary source: Apple DTS (Quinn), forums/788807, to a developer whose build failed with 'Provisioning profile doesn't include the com.apple.developer.wifi-aware entitlement' — 'Are you a member of a paid team? Many capabilities are only available to paid teams... [the table] hasn't been updated to cover the Wi-Fi Aware capability yet (r. 153813100) but, when it is, I suspect that there will only be checks in the first two columns.' The developer confirmed the free team was the cause. Hardware floor: iPhone 12+, iPad 10th gen+, iPad Air 4+, iPad Pro 11" 3rd gen+/12.9" 5th gen+, iPad mini 6+. Not in the simulator; macOS 26 has no support. Like NearbyInteraction, it only finds devices running compatible services.

capabilities.stream: VPN / tunnel active state — free heuristic path
capabilities.api: (a) NWPath.unsatisfiedReason == .vpnInactive; (b) CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings() -> dictionary, inspect the '__SCOPED__' key for interface names matching tap / tun / ppp / ipsec / utun; (c) getifaddrs() interface-name scan for utun*/ipsec*/ppp*/tap*
capabilities.resolution: Pollable at any rate; event-driven for (a)
capabilities.notes: FREE-TEAM COMPATIBLE and the only VPN visibility a sideloaded app actually gets. CONTESTED — do not treat interface presence as proof: iOS creates utun interfaces for reasons other than a user VPN (iCloud Private Relay, Continuity/Handoff, system tunnels), so a bare 'utun0 exists' check yields false positives. The defensible method is correlation: require BOTH a tunnel-named interface AND a matching entry under CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings()['__SCOPED__']. Second gap: split-tunnel and some OpenVPN-style clients ride a mix of en0 and utun*, producing false negatives. WireGuard on iOS runs as an NEPacketTunnelProvider and does surface as utun*.

capabilities.stream: VPN configuration and connection status — supported path
capabilities.api: NEVPNManager.shared() + loadFromPreferences; .isEnabled, .localizedDescription, .protocolConfiguration, .isOnDemandEnabled, .onDemandRules, .connection -> NEVPNConnection.status -> NEVPNStatus (.invalid, .disconnected, .connecting, .connected, .reasserting, .disconnecting); NEVPNStatusDidChange notification. Also NETunnelProviderManager.loadAllFromPreferences(completionHandler:)
capabilities.notes: PAID ONLY — 'Personal VPN' and 'Network extensions' are both blank in the free column of Apple's table. AND it does not do what you want: these APIs surface only configurations YOUR app created. You cannot read the WireGuard app's tunnel state, or any other app's, at any membership tier. For 'is my own WireGuard up', the free heuristic path above is strictly better than the paid one.

capabilities.stream: Personal Hotspot — this device is SHARING its connection
capabilities.api: getifaddrs() presence of bridge100 (and ap1); corroborate with NWPath.availableInterfaces names; byte counters on bridge100 measure how much clients pulled
capabilities.notes: Undocumented heuristic — Apple DTS says BSD interface names are not API. bridge100 appears when iOS bridges pdp_ip0 to the USB/Bluetooth/Wi-Fi client interface for tethering.

capabilities.stream: Personal Hotspot — this device is TETHERED TO someone else's
capabilities.notes: Rests on Apple's own documented semantics for isExpensive ('Cellular or a Personal Hotspot'), so this is a documented inference rather than a hack — Wi-Fi that is also expensive is by definition a hotspot. Fully free.

capabilities.stream: Bluetooth radio power state and app-level Bluetooth authorization
capabilities.notes: A free behavioural stream in its own right: how often and when the user toggles Bluetooth off. CBManager.authorization can be read WITHOUT instantiating a manager, so you can check authorization without triggering the prompt.

capabilities.stream: Apple Watch reachability and its own independent network path
capabilities.api: WCSession.default.isReachable, .activationState, .isPaired, .isWatchAppInstalled, .isComplicationEnabled, WCSessionDelegate.sessionReachabilityDidChange(_:); on watchOS: NWPathMonitor (watchOS 5+), NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent (watchOS 7+), CTTelephonyNetworkInfo on cellular Watch models
capabilities.notes: Non-obvious and free: WCSession.isReachable flips based on whether the Watch and iPhone can talk right now — a decent 'watch on wrist and within ~10 m' proximity series, plus a de-facto 'phone left behind' detector when the Watch stays reachable over Wi-Fi but not Bluetooth. The Watch also runs its own NWPathMonitor, so a cellular Watch gives you a genuinely SECOND, independent network vantage point at the same instant.

blockers: FREE APPLE ID CANNOT READ THE WI-FI SSID OR BSSID. AT ALL. The single biggest constraint in the domain. Apple's supported-capabilities table (developer.apple.com/help/account/reference/supported-capabilities-ios) has three columns — ADP, ADEP, and 'Apple Developer' (= the free Personal Team, confirmed by Apple DTS at developer.apple.com/forums/thread/746373: 'The rightmost column in the table lists the thing you can do with a free account (aka a Personal Team)'). Parsing the raw page markup, the free column is checked for EXACTLY NINE capabilities: App groups, Background modes, Data protection, HealthKit, HomeKit, Inter-App Audio, Keychain sharing, Maps, Wireless Accessory Configuration. 'Access WiFi information' is NOT among them. Consequence: NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent and CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo return nil forever on a free-signed build, no matter what location permission is granted. The $99/yr Apple Developer Program is the only fix.

Also blank in the free column, therefore unsignable on a free Apple ID: Network extensions (com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension), Personal VPN (com.apple.developer.networking.vpn.api), Multipath (com.apple.developer.networking.multipath), Hotspot/HotspotConfiguration, 5G Network Slicing, NFC Tag Reading, Media Device Discovery, Sustained Execution, Push notifications, App Attest, Associated Domains, iCloud, Sign in with Apple. Apple DTS, asked 'can I add Network Extensions without joining the program': 'No.'

Wi-Fi Aware (iOS 26's flagship networking addition) is paid-only despite being absent from the capability table. Apple DTS, forums/788807: 'Many capabilities are only available to paid teams... [the table] hasn't been updated to cover the Wi-Fi Aware capability yet (r. 153813100) but, when it is, I suspect that there will only be checks in the first two columns.' The reporting developer confirmed a free team caused his build failure. Flagged as strong-inference-plus-DTS-statement rather than table-verified.

SCANNING FOR NEARBY WI-FI NETWORKS IS IMPOSSIBLE AT EVERY TIER. No public API on any iOS version, free or paid, returns a list of visible access points. The only surface that ever exposed a scan list is NEHotspotHelper, and it delivers networks only inside helper command callbacks while the system Wi-Fi picker is engaged.

NEHotspotHelper is effectively unobtainable. Paid team PLUS manual Apple approval via developer.apple.com/contact/request/hotspot-helper. Apple DTS: 'The vast majority of Hotspot Helper requests are rejected because they are not a support use case for the API' and it 'is only useful for hotspot integration. There are both technical and business restrictions that prevent it from being used for other tasks, such as accessory integration or Wi-Fi based location.' Wi-Fi-based location logging is named as a disqualifying use. Turnaround weeks to months.

CARRIER IDENTITY IS PERMANENTLY GONE. CTCarrier is deprecated with no replacement and, for anything built with the iOS 16.4 SDK or later, returns static garbage: carrierName and isoCountryCode = '--', mobileCountryCode and mobileNetworkCode = '65535'. Apple's own 16.4 beta release note documents this (radar 76283818). Verified still the case in the iOS 26/27 era. Asked directly for an alternative, Apple DTS answered: 'No. That's what Deprecated with no replacement means.' Do not put a carrier column in the schema. What DID survive: serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology (5G NR/NSA, LTE, etc.) and dataServiceIdentifier.

Whole-device, cross-reboot data usage — the number the Settings app shows — has no supported API. Apple DTS states that getting 'whole device statistics that persist across a restart' has no supported solution. getifaddrs resets to zero on every reboot, so you can only reconstruct usage for the current boot session.

Per-app data usage for OTHER apps is impossible and will never exist. Apple DTS: 'iOS isolates your app from other apps, so you're unlikely to get an API that returns per-app statistics for all apps on the system.' MetricKit gives you only your own app's numbers.

getifaddrs byte counters are UInt32 and WRAP AT 4 GiB, and if_data64 is unreachable: 'The <net/if_var.h> header defines an if_data64 structure, but there's no supported way to get that value on Apple platforms.' On modern Wi-Fi a 4 GiB wrap is a daily event, not a corner case — a sampler that does not detect and correct wraps will silently under-report. Apple adds: 'Due to its legacy nature, there's little point filing an enhancement request against this API.'

CoreBluetooth CANNOT SEE YOUR CAR, YOUR AIRPODS, OR MOST SPEAKERS. CoreBluetooth is BLE-only; those devices connect over classic Bluetooth BR/EDR using A2DP/HFP. There is no public API to enumerate classic BT connections. The workaround is AVAudioSession.currentRoute (portType .carAudio / .bluetoothA2DP / .bluetoothHFP plus the literal portName), which is free and permissionless — but it shows only devices in the current AUDIO route, so a connected-but-silent device may not appear.

Background BLE scanning with nil service UUIDs returns nothing. Apple verbatim: 'your app must explicitly scan for one or more services by specifying them in the serviceUUIDs parameter. The CBCentralManager scan option has no effect while scanning in the background.' The 'count everything nearby as a crowd proxy' technique is therefore FOREGROUND-ONLY. Background scanning is additionally throttled by undocumented power heuristics that vary by device model, OS version and battery state — Apple describes it as eventual, not real-time.

You cannot count PEOPLE from BLE. iOS and Android rotate BLE addresses roughly every 15 minutes, and CBPeripheral.identifier is scoped to your-app-on-this-device, so there is no stable identity for a stranger's phone across sessions or across devices. Apple devices also stuff most service UUIDs into CBAdvertisementDataOverflowServiceUUIDsKey, discoverable only by explicitly scanning for those exact UUIDs. Any crowd number is a relative index, never a headcount.

You cannot read another app's VPN state. NEVPNManager and NETunnelProviderManager surface only configurations your own app created — true at every membership tier. There is no API that reports 'the WireGuard app's tunnel is up.' Free heuristics (utun interface + CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings __SCOPED__) are the only option and are unreliable in both directions.

Wi-Fi signal strength is not available. NEHotspotNetwork.signalStrength exists but Apple states fetchCurrent 'doesn't populate other fields in the object' — it is filled only inside an NEHotspotHelper callback, which you will not get approved. Cellular signal strength in dBm or bars has no public API at all; reading it requires private CoreTelephony SPI or status-bar scraping. NWPath.linkQuality (iOS 26, 4 coarse levels) is the only public substitute.

There is no API to query local-network permission status. You must attempt a Bonjour browse and infer from failure or timeout. NWPath.unsatisfiedReason == .localNetworkDenied is the closest official signal and appears only when a path is actually blocked. Known misbehaviour in iOS 17.x–18.x: denial sometimes does not take effect until reboot, and in some 18.x builds communication continued despite an explicit deny — verify empirically on your own device rather than trusting the setting.

Browsing ARBITRARY Bonjour service types, or sending/receiving IP multicast or broadcast, requires com.apple.developer.networking.multicast, which Apple's own doc says 'requires permission from Apple' via the form at developer.apple.com/contact/request/networking-multicast, on top of a paid membership. Without it you must enumerate every service type in NSBonjourServices at build time.

FREE PROVISIONING EXPIRES EVERY 7 DAYS. A Personal Team provisioning profile is valid for 7 days; when it lapses the app simply stops launching until you rebuild and redeploy from Xcode. Limits are 10 App IDs and 3 registered devices, each also on a 7-day clock. For a long-horizon logging app this is a real operational tax — accept a weekly re-sign (AltStore/SideStore can automate the refresh), or pay the $99. TrollStore-style entitlement injection does not work on iOS 26/27.
MultipeerConnectivity is deprecated in its entirety — every major class carries a deprecation marker. Do not build new peer-discovery work on it.

iOS 27 (developer beta 4 as of 2026-07-20, GA expected September 2026) deprecates MXNetworkTransferMetric in favour of MetricManager / MetricResult with TotalWiFiDownloadMetric, TotalWiFiUploadMetric, TotalCellularDownloadMetric, TotalCellularUploadMetric. Building only against MXNetworkTransferMetric puts your byte-history stream on a deprecation clock. Two unrelated iOS 27 SDK gates also apply: apps built with the iOS 27 SDK must include a launch screen, and must adopt the UIKit scene-based lifecycle or they fail to launch.
nonObvious: THE $99 DECISION IS THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE, AND IT IS BINARY. Everything Wi-Fi-identity — SSID, BSSID, Captive Network, Wi-Fi Aware, Network Extension, Personal VPN, Multipath — sits behind capabilities Apple's own table checks only for ADP/ADEP. Everything else in this domain (NWPathMonitor and all its properties, all 13 radio-access-technology constants, getifaddrs, MetricKit, URLSession metrics, CoreBluetooth, NearbyInteraction, Bonjour browsing, AVAudioSession routes, WatchConnectivity) is free. Decide this before writing a line of code, because the free and paid architectures fingerprint 'place' in completely different ways.

NWInterface.name IS A FREE SIDE CHANNEL AND ALMOST NOBODY USES IT. NWPath.availableInterfaces hands you the raw BSD names with no permission and no entitlement. From names alone: tunnel active (utun*/ipsec*/ppp*), Apple peer-to-peer activity such as AirDrop/AirPlay/Handoff in progress (awdl0 up), this device is SHARING a hotspot (bridge100/ap1), and which SIM is carrying data (pdp_ip0 vs pdp_ip1). Apple DTS notes BSD names are not formally API, so treat them as heuristics — but they cost nothing and no entitlement gates them.

usesInterfaceType(.wifi) && isExpensive == true IS A DOCUMENTED HOTSPOT DETECTOR. Apple's own abstract for isExpensive says 'Cellular or a Personal Hotspot.' Wi-Fi that is simultaneously expensive can only be a Personal Hotspot. That is an inference from Apple's stated semantics, not a hack — and it cleanly separates 'I am tethered to someone' from 'I am sharing to someone' (bridge100).

AVAudioSession.currentRoute.outputs[].portName IS THE REAL ANSWER TO 'WHAT BLUETOOTH DEVICES AM I CONNECTED TO' — no permission, no prompt, no entitlement. It returns the literal user-visible names ('Zach's AirPods Pro', 'Honda HFT'), with portType distinguishing .bluetoothA2DP / .bluetoothHFP / .carAudio / .airPlay. Most developers reach for CoreBluetooth here and get nothing, because cars and AirPods are classic BR/EDR and CoreBluetooth is BLE-only. Observing routeChangeNotification with the 'audio' background mode gives a continuous free device-attachment log — and .carAudio is a near-perfect driving detector.

BONJOUR ENUMERATION IS THE FREE REPLACEMENT FOR BSSID FINGERPRINTING. You cannot read the SSID on a free account, but NWBrowser (iOS 26: NetworkBrowser) over a declared list of service types returns the actual set of devices on the LAN — Apple TVs, HomePods, printers, NAS, other Macs. Hash that set and you have a per-place identifier with far more entropy than the gateway IP, for one plist string and one runtime prompt. Cross-check with NWPath.gateways and supportsIPv6 to harden against a device being powered off.

getifaddrs GIVES YOU FREE BACKFILL AND A FREE REBOOT CLOCK. Its counters are cumulative since last restart, so your very first sample on launch already contains the whole boot session's traffic — the only backfill in this domain besides MetricKit. And because they reset on reboot, a counter DECREASE is itself a signal: cross-check ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime to distinguish a reboot from a 4 GiB UInt32 wrap (add 2^32 in the wrap case). You get a device-uptime and reboot-frequency series free out of the same sampler.

THE ONLY RELIABLE FREE WAY TO RUN A NETWORK SAMPLER 24/7 IS THE LOCATION BACKGROUND MODE. NWPathMonitor, getifaddrs and CoreTelephony have no background mode of their own — iOS suspends your process within ~30 s of backgrounding and every one of those streams goes dark. Background Modes IS free-team signable, so the practical pattern is: 'location' background mode + Always authorization (significant-location-change or a low-accuracy region monitor keeps the process resident indefinitely), then sample the network streams from inside that runtime. 'bluetooth-central' only wakes you on matched service UUIDs; 'audio' with a silent loop also works and is fine for a sideloaded personal app though it would never survive App Review. BGAppRefreshTask/BGProcessingTask give only sparse opportunistic windows.

MetricKit IS THE ONLY SUPPORTED BYTE COUNTER AND IT IS FREE. No entitlement, no permission, works on a Personal Team, and Apple DTS names it as the sanctioned answer to 'how much data did I use.' Cost: 24-hour aggregation delivered at most once per day, and only for your own app. Pair it with getifaddrs — MetricKit for the trustworthy daily total, getifaddrs for the second-by-second shape.

FETCHCURRENT HAS THREE DOORS BESIDES LOCATION PERMISSION. Apple's documented alternatives to precise-location authorization are: your app configured the network via NEHotspotConfiguration, your app has active VPN configurations installed, or your app has an active NEDNSSettingsManager configuration. All are paid entitlements so none is a free workaround — but if you are already paying and already ship a DNS or VPN profile, you can read the SSID without ever asking for location.

BUILD YOUR OWN NETWORK-QUALITY INSTRUMENT WITH URLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics. A scheduled 1-byte request against a known endpoint yields DNS lookup time, TCP connect time, TLS handshake time, time-to-first-byte, negotiated HTTP version, remote IP, and isCellular/isExpensive/isConstrained/isMultipath — 11 timestamps and 6 byte counters per request, at zero permission cost. A richer connectivity-quality series than anything Apple exposes directly, and entirely free.

THE APPLE WATCH IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT NETWORK VANTAGE POINT. It runs its own NWPathMonitor (watchOS 5+), its own NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent (watchOS 7+), and on cellular models its own CTTelephonyNetworkInfo. Simultaneous paired samples distinguish 'the network is down' from 'the phone specifically lost the network.' Separately, WCSession.isReachable is a free permissionless proximity series that flips as the Watch moves in and out of range — doubling as a 'phone left behind' detector.

CTCellularData.restrictedState DISAMBIGUATES 'NO SIGNAL' FROM 'NO PERMISSION.' Free, no prompt, with a change notifier. Combine with a nil entry in serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology (which means that service is not registered on any network) to tell apart: user disabled cellular for this app; cellular is on but has no service; cellular is fine.

ENUMERATE STANDARD SIG SERVICE UUIDS TO GET AROUND retrieveConnectedPeripherals' DESIGN. There is no 'list everything connected' call — you must pass service UUIDs. Calling retrieveConnectedPeripherals repeatedly across a table of well-known SIG UUIDs (0x180D heart rate, 0x180F battery, 0x1812 HID, 0x1816 cycling speed, 0x1826 fitness machine, and so on) recovers a usable inventory of connected BLE devices — including ones connected by other apps, which Apple explicitly confirms are included.

AccessorySetupKit (iOS 18+) LETS YOU SKIP THE BLUETOOTH AND LOCAL-NETWORK PROMPTS ENTIRELY for accessories you declare up front — the picker itself is the consent. Info.plist-only, no entitlement, so free-team compatible. It narrows visibility rather than widening it: right tool for your own known devices, wrong tool for crowd sensing.

VPN DETECTION NEEDS TWO SIGNALS, NOT ONE. Presence of a utun interface alone produces false positives — iOS creates utun interfaces for iCloud Private Relay and Continuity, not just user VPNs. Require both a tunnel-named interface AND a matching entry under CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings()['__SCOPED__'], and know that split-tunnel clients riding a mix of en0 and utun* still produce false negatives. NWPath.unsatisfiedReason == .vpnInactive is the only signal here Apple actually documents.

CONTESTED POINT WORTH KNOWING: the folklore that App Groups are unavailable to free Personal Teams is WRONG. Apple's table checks App groups in the free column. So is Background modes, HealthKit and HomeKit — which means a free-signed app can hold background execution modes and write its network telemetry into a shared container and even into HealthKit. Multiple secondary sources online state the opposite; the primary table is authoritative.

DO NOT TRUST WEB SUMMARIES OF APPLE'S DOCS FOR VERSION OR ENTITLEMENT FACTS. During this research both a search summary and a page summarizer got the capability table exactly backwards (reporting every capability as available to free accounts), and Apple's own NWPath list page renders iOS 26 additions as 'iOS 12.0+'. The reliable method is fetching the per-symbol JSON at developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/<path>.json, or parsing the raw HTML directly. Every version number and entitlement claim above was pulled that way.
